title: A vector built to its specification
hints: Write one private `reallocate(newCapacity)` that allocates, copies the existing elements and swaps the new block in. Every growth rule in the table is then a single line deciding the new capacity.
Check every precondition before you change anything, and allocate before you overwrite the old block: then "unchanged when they throw" holds even if the allocation itself throws.
Copy and move assignment are easiest as "make a new vector, then swap it with `*this`": self-assignment and cleanup of the old block then take care of themselves.
requirements: Every constructor, assignment and member behaves as its row of the reference says, including returned indices.
Capacity follows the growth rules exactly, and `data()` stays the same when no reallocation is due.
Out-of-range calls throw the documented exception and leave the vector unchanged.
Copies are independent; moved-from vectors are empty.
No leaks and no use of `std::vector` inside the class.
